newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa may take first steps since surgery.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa may take first steps since surgery.

text.p: Mother Teresa was expected to try to take her first steps on Wednesday since undergoing life-saving heart surgery last week, doctors said.
The B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre in Calcutta said experts from the physical therapy department would work with the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun.
"Physical therapy will attempt to get her up for a walk this afternoon," clinic official A.K. Chatterjee said, reading a medical bulletin.
Mother Teresa, revered for her life-long devotion to the destitute and dying, has been suffering from an irregular heartbeat, bronchial pneumonia and weak kidneys.
The 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner underwent surgery last week to clear two blocked arteries and had appeared to be recovering when longstanding kidney and lung problems resurfaced.

Her vital signs were stable on Wednesday, but her health remained at risk, doctors said. Her heart continued to beat irregularly and her kidneys remained weak, the bulletin said, but her lungs had improved.
"This morning she asked the doctors to let her rest since they had made her work hard all night with respiratory therapy," the statement said without elaborating.
Mother Teresa's appetite was not very good on Wednesday morning, the doctors said. She had some papaya, bread and orange juice for breakfast, Chatterjee said.
"Today she had Horlicks for the first time," he added, referring to the energy-enriching drink. "She is 86 years old and everything has to be kept in a favourable equilibrium."
An earlier bulletin said Mother Teresa had talked with sisters from her Missionaries of Charity order in the morning. She sat up in a chair and listened to mass, it said.
On Tuesday doctors said they were optimistic she would recover, but cautioned that it would be a slow process and she might never be as active as before.

Despite a series of health problems, Mother Teresa had kept up a seemingly tireless pace in her religious order and travelled widely before her latest illness. Her Missionaries of Charity order runs 456 homes in 111 countries.
The nun, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, had her first heart operation in the United States in 1991 and her second at the Birla centre in 1993.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda planned to make a special trip to Calcutta on Thursday to visit Mother Teresa in the clinic, his office said.
